english.title: Engage in conduct likely to assist a foreign intelligence service
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) engaged in conduct, namely **(..SPECIFY CONDUCT..), that was likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service carrying out UK-related activities, when you knew, or having regard to other matters known to you, ought to have known, that the conduct was likely to materially assist that service in carrying out those activities

english.notes:
(i) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Attorney General, section 37 of the National Security Act 2023.
(ii) This offence covers 'espionage' relating to conduct 'likely' to materially assist a foreign intelligence service. For the offence relating to conduct 'intended' to assist a foreign intelligence service, see H101393. For the offence relating to obtaining or disclosing of protected information in relation to the government’s sensitive information, see H101391. For the offence relating to obtaining/disclosing trade secrets, see H101392.
(iii) Conduct that may be likely to assist a foreign intelligence service includes providing (access to) information, goods, services or financial benefits, whether directly or indirectly, see section 3(3).(iv) This offence applies to conduct outside the United Kingdom, but to conduct taking place wholly outside the UK only where the person engaging in the conduct is a UK person or a person who acts for or on behalf of, or holds office under, the Crown, or is in Crown employment (whether or not they engage in the conduct in that capacity) (section 3(6)).(v) Section 3(7) provides defences to this offence, ensuring that certain conduct is not caught (for example, where an individual was acting as a lawyer carrying on a legal activity), with section 3(8) outlining there is an evidential burden in relation to the defences.
(vi) Additional powers of entry, search and seizure are provided in Schedule 2 where there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that this offence has been, or is about to be, committed.
